kurz: How trends, zones and breakouts can be defined in a testable way, and what empirical studies show about their usefulness.

bloecke.md:
A trend describes past price movement and is not a property of the market. It only becomes visible after it has formed, and it ends before anyone declares it over. With this caveat, trend descriptions can be used as a framework for organising risk. They are of no use as a promise about the future course of prices.

Technical analysis derives its statements exclusively from the history of prices and volumes. It says nothing about the value of a company; it models the behaviour of market participants. That is not a flaw, but it limits the scope of its statements, and this limit must be borne in mind in every application.

The oldest systematised chart theory comes from Charles Dow's editorials and not from a book. William Peter Hamilton continued these editorials, and Robert Rhea later organised them. According to the core tenets of the theory, the index reflects everything that is publicly known. There are three degrees of trend: the primary trend over years, the secondary correction over weeks to months and the tertiary movement over days. A primary trend passes through three phases: accumulation, broad participation and distribution. Two indices must confirm each other (originally industrial and railway shares). Volume should support the direction. Finally, a trend is considered intact until there is a clear reversal signal. The fact that it becomes uncomfortable for the investor is not such a signal.

The theory has been tested empirically several times. Alfred Cowles declared it a failure in 1933. In 1998, Brown, Goetzmann and Kumar re-examined this refutation and came to the opposite conclusion. According to their analysis, Hamilton's commentaries from 1902 to 1929 achieved high Sharpe ratios and positive alphas. This is a historical finding about a single author with strong judgement, from which no transferable set of rules can be derived.

## Defining a trend by highs and lows

Without room for interpretation, a trend can only be defined by means of extreme points. A *swing high* is a high that is framed on the left and right by n lower highs each (two or three are common). A swing low is, correspondingly, a low framed on the left and right by n higher lows each. An uptrend exists when both the swing highs and the swing lows are rising. If either of the two conditions is missing, it is a sideways movement, even if the chart looks positive.

The same definition provides the criterion for the end of the trend. First, the structure of lows breaks, that is, a low forms below the last relevant low. A lower high afterwards confirms the break but is not a condition for it. An exit based on gut feeling or at a round loss figure, by contrast, rests on no fixed rule.

The timeframe plays an important role here. The same price series can show a downtrend on the daily chart and a correction within an uptrend on the weekly chart. That is not a contradiction; both findings result from different filters. If you switch the timeframe when the findings conflict, however, that is no longer analysis, because you are then picking the answer that suits you.

bloecke.md: The end of a trend shows in the price structure and not in how you feel. As long as the last relevant low holds, the uptrend is intact, even if the candles look uncomfortable. If this low is broken, the trend is over, even if the reasoning behind the investment still sounds convincing.

## Support and resistance as zones

Support and resistance are price ranges in which orders accumulate, not exact lines. Three mechanisms explain why trading takes place precisely there.

The first mechanism is the entry prices of earlier buyers. At an earlier high, many shares changed hands. Investors who bought there and have been sitting on a loss ever since offer their shares as soon as the price reaches their entry price again.

The second mechanism is the **disposition effect**. Using around 10,000 securities accounts (1987-1993), Odean measured that winning positions are realised with a probability of 14.8%, losing positions with only 9.8%. Winners are thus sold around one and a half times as often as losers, and their own entry price keeps investors from selling at a loss. The same study also found that the winners sold went on to outperform the losers held by an average of 3.4 percentage points in the following year. The behaviour therefore creates the zone and at the same time costs return.

The third mechanism is self-fulfilment. Many chart readers see the same level and place their orders there. As a result, the level becomes effective for a while, without the direction of the subsequent move being determined. Below a popular support level there is a cluster of stop-loss orders, which accelerate a fall in price as soon as they are triggered.

In practice, the zone covers the range in which the previous bounces occurred. With highs of 128 and 129, it extends from 128 to 129 and is not to be understood as a single line. The later high of 131 lies above the zone and marks the false breakout.

bloecke.titel: Realisation rates for winning and losing positions
bloecke.unter: Share of positions that are sold (Odean, around 10,000 US securities accounts, 1987-1993). The gap between the two values is the excess supply that a chart shows as a zone.

## Round numbers

Zones are strikingly often found at round amounts such as €100 per share, 20,000 index points or 1.10 for an exchange rate. The cause lies in the perception of market participants and not in the market. In 1974, Tversky and Kahneman used a rigged wheel of fortune to show how strongly a seemingly random number shifts estimates. With an anchor of 10, participants estimated the share of African countries in the UN at 25%; with an anchor of 65, at 45%. Limit and stop orders are placed according to the same pattern at numbers that are easy to say.

This results in a clustering of orders, but not automatically in an advantage. That orders cluster at round levels is a behavioural observation. Whether a profit can be made from this after spread, fees and taxes is another question, and empirically it is the more difficult one.

## Breakout and false breakout

A breakout is only defined once it has been established which price, in which timeframe, has to lie how far outside the zone. Without these three specifications, a breakout remains a mere impression. The usual approach is to work with closing prices and a minimum distance.

bloecke.formel: Breakout confirmed if Closing price > Upper zone limit × (1 + f)
bloecke.erklaerung: The only effect of the filter f is that fewer signals arise, and that is its purpose. Every filter worsens the entry price and cuts off part of the movement. These disadvantages are the price of fewer signals and not a design flaw.
variablen: highest price of the previous bounces, not the average
minimum distance, typically 0.5% to 2% depending on volatility
close of the chosen timeframe, not a price during the session
bloecke.beispiel: With a zone up to 129 points and f = 1%, the breakout only counts from a closing price above 130.29 points. A daily high of 133 with a close of 130 does not count.

bloecke.md:
A false breakout occurs when the price leaves the zone and returns to it within a few periods. The return systematically takes the price into the area where the breakout buyers' stop orders are placed. That is why a false breakout often moves fast and far.

The rule for this case is set before entry and not only afterwards. If the thesis “close above the zone” no longer holds, the reason for the position no longer holds either. Buying more while in a loss turns a defined risk into an undefined one. Moving the stop down does the same, only more slowly.

## State of research on breakout rules

Breakout rules are among the best-studied parts of technical analysis, and the course of the research is more revealing than any single result. In 1992, Brock, Lakonishok and LeBaron found strong evidence for simple moving average and breakout rules in the Dow from 1897 to 1986. In 1999, Sullivan, Timmermann and White used a bootstrap procedure to test the winning rule together with the entire universe of rules from which it had been selected. For 1897 to 1986, the results withstood this test, but in the ten years that followed (1987 to 1996) even the best rule no longer delivered a significant advantage. Bajgrowicz and Scaillet confirmed this in 2012 using false discovery methods. After correcting for multiple testing and with realistic transaction costs, practically nothing remains, and the rules that were successful in the past are not persistent.

Park and Irwin's review counts 95 modern studies, 56 of them with positive, 20 with negative and 19 with mixed results. The authors counter this by pointing out that most studies suffer from rule selection after the fact and overly favourable cost assumptions. In practice, this means that trend and zone are suitable as concepts for describing risk. They are of little use as a basis for an expectation of returns.

bloecke.titel: Illustrative calculation with €100,000 and 250 round turns a year
bloecke.unter: The friction of 0.10% per round turn (fee, half the spread on each side, slippage) costs 25 percentage points a year. Tax is only calculated on the remaining result.

bloecke.md:
When trading breakouts, gains and losses are realised continuously. Under Section 32d(1) EStG (Income Tax Act), the flat-rate withholding tax (Abgeltungsteuer) of 25% applies, plus a solidarity surcharge of 5.5% on it, together 26.375%. With church tax, it is around 27.82% (at 8% church tax) or 27.99% (at 9%). The only deduction is the saver's allowance (Sparer-Pauschbetrag) of €1,000 per person (Section 20(9) EStG). Actual income-related expenses (Werbungskosten) such as charting software or custody fees are not deductible.

For traders, Section 20(6) sentence 4 EStG is particularly important. Under it, losses from sales of shares may only be offset against gains from sales of shares. If an investor realises a loss of €8,000 on shares and a gain of €8,000 on an index certificate in the same year, the two do not offset each other for tax purposes. Before deduction of the allowance, tax of €2,110 is due on the certificate gain, and the share loss is carried forward without time limit. The former €20,000 limit for derivative transactions (Termingeschäfte) was abolished without replacement by the Annual Tax Act 2024 (Jahressteuergesetz) and no longer appears in the text of the law.

The statement “The zone works because everyone believes in it” sounds like proof, but it can also be turned against the zone. A level that exists only through shared expectation is most crowded when many market participants are positioned the same way. If the level breaks in this situation, the same positions amplify the countermovement.

The search for mathematically special levels has so far been unsuccessful. Batchelor and Ramyar examined whether the length and duration ratios of successive trends in the Dow cluster around Fibonacci ratios. They found only as many significant cases as would be expected by chance given the number of tests carried out. This is only a single working paper, but its result points in the same direction as all the other findings. Zones are therefore an observation about the concentration of orders and not a law.

- Require at least two touches as evidence; a single point can be chance.
- Note the upper and lower limits as a range, not as a line.
- Fix the timeframe and do not change it while the position is open.
- Note which closing price confirms the breakout (formula above).
- Before entry, note which closing price refutes the thesis.
- Decide after how many weeks without a touch the zone expires and is deleted.

All rules must be fixed before entry; rules drawn up later do not serve their purpose.

mitnehmen: An uptrend consists of higher swing highs and higher swing lows; it breaks first in the structure of lows and not according to feeling.
Support and resistance are zones and not lines; they arise from the entry prices of earlier buyers, the disposition effect (realisation rate of 14.8% versus 9.8%) and shared expectation.
Round numbers work through the anchoring effect and explain where orders are placed, but not that you can make money from them.
A breakout needs a definition of timeframe, closing price and minimum distance, otherwise it remains an impression; a false breakout refutes the thesis instead of merely postponing it.
The strong breakout findings of 1992 have largely disappeared after correcting for multiple testing and costs; with 250 round turns, trading costs alone amount to 25 percentage points a year.

begriffe.text: High that is framed on the left and right by several lower highs each. Only the specified number of neighbouring bars turns a high into a testable statement.
Price range in which sell orders accumulate, usually around earlier highs and round numbers. It is given as a range and not as a line, because the bounces are scattered.
Movement in which the price leaves a zone and returns to it within a few periods. The breakout thesis is thus refuted and not merely postponed.
Minimum distance or minimum duration from which leaving the zone counts as a breakout. The filter reduces false signals and at the same time worsens the entry price.

Oldest systematised chart theory, which emerged from the editorials of Dow and Hamilton. It distinguishes three degrees of trend and three phases and requires confirmation by a second index and by volume.
